section_equality_counterexample.data: Take a field κ, S=V=Spec(κ), E=κ², B=κ[x_0,x_1] with both variables of degree1, X=P¹_κ, F=O_X, truncation k=0, s=x_0, d=1 and n=2. These are within the source projective-bundle setting.
section_equality_counterexample.right: D_+(x_0)=Spec(κ[t]), t=x_1/x_0. The section x_0² trivializes O(2) there, and Γ(D_+(x_0),O(2))=κ[t]x_0².
section_equality_counterexample.exact_restriction: a x_0²+b x_0x_1+c x_1² maps to (a+b t+c t²)x_0². The target section t³x_0² has no preimage because equality with a polynomial of degree≤2 would give the nonzero polynomial t³−c t²−b t−a=0 in κ[t].
section_equality_counterexample.conclusion: The canonical restriction is not surjective, so the asserted equality cannot be the canonical identification required by the construction. The explicit finite-dimensional source and infinite-dimensional target also preclude a κ-linear isomorphism.

separate_truncation_example.data: Keep S, E, X, F, s, d and n as above, but set the source truncation integer k=3.
separate_truncation_example.calculation: M_2=0 by the direct-sum definition, whereas Γ(D_+(x_0),O(2))=κ[t]x_0² is nonzero. Also H⁰(P¹,O(2)) is nonzero. Thus replacing only D_+(V,s) by f^(-1)V would still fail as an unconditional equality at this degree.
separate_truncation_example.fraction_scope: The only numerator in degree2 of this truncated M is zero. A fraction can be represented with denominator exponent n+N by replacing its numerator z with s^N z; choosing N large makes (n+N)d≥k. This degree adjustment is part of a full explanation, not a fact printed in the disputed equality.

actual_canonical_map.component_map: There is a canonical degreewise map j_nd:M_nd→f_*F(nd), identity on the indicated component for nd≥k and the zero-source map for nd<k.
actual_canonical_map.restriction: By the definition of direct image, Γ(V,f_*F(nd))=Γ(f^(-1)V,F(nd)). Restriction along D=D_+(V,s)⊂f^(-1)V gives ρ:Γ(f^(-1)V,F(nd))→Γ(D,F(nd)).
actual_canonical_map.fraction_map: Send z/s^n to a^(-n)ρ(j_nd(z)), where a=α_d(s)|D and a^n=α_nd(s^n)|D. This is a section of F on D.
actual_canonical_map.well_definedness: Equality z/s^n=z-prime/s^m means s^N(s^m z−s^n z-prime)=0 for some N. Compatibility of j and restriction with the B-action sends this to a^N(a^mρ(j_nd(z))−a^nρ(j_md(z-prime)))=0 on D. Multiplying by the inverse trivialization a^(-(N+m+n)) proves equality of the two resulting F-sections. The same formula commutes with restriction in V and with the degree-zero localized B-action.
actual_canonical_map.finite_degree_example: In the k=0 example, x_1²/x_0² maps to t². The target t³ is obtained from the degree3 numerator x_1³ with denominator x_0³. Localization permits varying the numerator degree; it does not identify the fixed degree2 source with all chart sections.
